_about: Hand-maintained input to build_known_effects.py. Predictions and test plans reasoned from code reading in one chat session (2026-11-28). They are NOT part of research/calibration-map and have NOT been run on hardware. Every item carries evidence 'predicted, untested' and is kept apart from the map's own traced/observed rules. Edit this file, then regenerate data/known_effects.json (README section 7).
source: chat-session code reading, 2026-11-28; cross-checked against research/calibration-map/map.json; not in that map; not bench-tested

GPS_DATA_SOURCE.text: In com.gm.server.timeofday.TimeofDayService (package CriticalWKSApp), value 2 selects a vehicle-property time source (VendorProperty.UTC, telematics-fed) and value 1 selects the location-fix time of GMLocationClient, a separate GM system service (IGMLocationService), not the standard Android LocationManager. Prediction: with the telematics/OnStar module disconnected, setting this to 1 may let the clock auto-correct from a location fix instead of the stale vehicle property. Prediction for the two BACK_OFFICE_SERVER_ENABLED cases, built on map rules settings.time.auto_datetime_row and time.trusted_clock_sync: (a) left at its bench value 1, Settings hides the Automatic Date / Time row and writes auto_time = 0 at its start-up, and the service still applies the trusted time but as trusted time minus the stored persist.sys.clockOffset, so the clock comes out right only if that offset is 0; (b) set to 0 as well, the row stays, auto_time can remain 1 and the service resets the offset to 0, so the clock follows trusted time directly. Neither case is blocked by the service itself: it does not read BACK_OFFICE_SERVER_ENABLED and no auto_time branch skips the clock write.
uncertainties: Not run on hardware, in either combination. Whether any location provider delivers fixes to GMLocationClient with value 1 on this bench is unknown; the calibration map lists the same question as unknown. Without a fix neither combination corrects anything.

Architectural: GMLocationClient / IGMLocationService is a GM-specific path, separate from the standard Android location stack. A working position in another app does not show that this path has a fix. See GNSS_DR_SRC.

Case (a) depends on runtime state the map does not hold: the stored persist.sys.clockOffset. A manual time entry made while no trusted time was available stores an offset against the remote real-time clock, and that offset stays applied when trusted time arrives. A new manual entry, or one switch of auto_time to 1, replaces it.
Case (b) changes every other rule that has BACK_OFFICE_SERVER_ENABLED as a term (Wi-Fi station, Settings rows); those side effects are not part of this prediction.
Whether the AOSP time detectors also write the clock is recorded in the calibration map as unknown.
That the vehicle property UTC is fed by the telematics module is recorded in the calibration map as inferred, not traced.
GPS_DATA_SOURCE.suggested_test: Bench, telematics module disconnected: record 'getprop persist.sys.clockOffset' and 'settings get global auto_time', set to 1, reboot, watch for 'VehicleTime: Trusted time verified and locked' and 'VehicleTime: Setting time to'; record the Settings date/time rows, the clock, the offset property and auto_time again. Repeat with BACK_OFFICE_SERVER_ENABLED = 0.

GNSS_DR_SRC.text: Selects which hardware the GM location / dead-reckoning subsystem sources from. Value 0 (bench and image) is 'TCP'. Value 1 was read in this session's decompiled code as 'ADR', explicitly named there for a u-blox GNSS chip.
uncertainties: Open question, not a finding: whether source 1 is the same physical GPS antenna leg that Google Maps already reads correctly on this bench. Maps uses the standard Android location stack; GNSS_DR_SRC and GMLocationClient govern a separate, GM-specific service.
GM's own CalDef enumeration labels value 1 'CSM', not 'ADR'; the 'ADR' / u-blox naming comes from the session's code reading only.
The calibration map has only established that this name is read (status 'read, effect not traced'); it records no effect for it.
Not run on hardware.

FM_RDS_Clocktime_enabled.text: Does NOT set the clock. Per LocalTimeHandler it is a fallback local-time source feeding automatic time zone detection only (that much is already the map's traced rule time.rds_local_source). Session additions: the fallback is itself gated behind a GPS-availability precondition, and the RDS path (vendor parameter com.gm.rds_time, read through GMTunerService from the tuner HAL) was never confirmed to decode on this hardware. Prediction: setting this to 1 will not by itself correct a wrong clock.
uncertainties: RDS decode on this hardware is unconfirmed: strings and symbols only, the HAL binary was not decompiled.
Not run on hardware; bench and image value is 0.

BACK_OFFICE_SERVER_ENABLED.text: In the Settings app's own eligibility check, isInternalGPSAvailable() requires this calibration to be OFF before 'Automatic date & time' is offered through the internal-GPS branch (GPS_DATA_SOURCE = 1). That is a different, stricter condition than TimeofDayService itself applies, which uses GPS_DATA_SOURCE alone and does not read this calibration. The Settings condition is already encoded in the map's traced rules for the two date/time rows; the Wi-Fi and other Settings effects of this calibration are the map rules listed for it and are not restated here. Untested consequence: at the bench value 1, changing GPS_DATA_SOURCE to 1 fails the Settings condition, so Settings writes auto_time = 0 at its start-up. Per map rule time.trusted_clock_sync that does not stop the service correcting the clock; it makes the service keep the stored persist.sys.clockOffset instead of resetting it to 0. Setting this calibration to 0 together with GPS_DATA_SOURCE = 1 keeps the condition true and is the combination predicted to follow trusted time with no stored offset. See the GPS_DATA_SOURCE note.
uncertainties: Not run on hardware. What the user-visible result is when Settings and the service disagree has not been observed.
The stored offset on the bench is unknown, and so is whether a location fix reaches the service with GPS_DATA_SOURCE = 1.

Apple_CarPlay_enableWireless.text: Turning BOTH Apple_CarPlay_enableWireless and AndroidAuto_enableWireless off should reveal the otherwise hidden 'Wi-Fi Services' manual hotspot control row. The visibility condition is already a traced map rule (ui.settings_wifi_services_menu); what is predicted and untested is the on-bench result of changing both from their bench value 1.
uncertainties: Not run on hardware.
Map rule wifi.hotspot_allowed (observed, true branch only) has the same two calibrations as terms: with both off its condition depends on hmi_hotspot_disable_status == 0.
Apple_CarPlay_enableWireless.suggested_test: Set both wireless calibrations to 0, open Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi hotspot and look for the Wi-Fi Services row.

uncertainties: Not run on hardware.

AndroidAuto_enableWireless.suggested_test: Set both wireless calibrations to 0, open Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi hotspot and look for the Wi-Fi Services row.

Enable_Application_Apple_Carplay.text: No new effect is predicted. The wired-attach gating through RDMSAppleStateMachine is the map's traced rule usb.apple_state_machine. Suggested bench test only: compare wired iPhone attach with this calibration on and off while both wireless calibrations are off, to separate GM's own wired handling from a kernel-level NCM claim.
uncertainties: A test plan, not a finding. The map notes that the effect on a kernel NCM driver is not shown by the code it traced.
Not run on hardware.
Enable_Application_Apple_Carplay.suggested_test: With Apple_CarPlay_enableWireless and AndroidAuto_enableWireless both 0, attach an iPhone by USB with this calibration 1, then 0; compare the 'ATTACH to AppleStateMachine sent' / 'RDMSAppleStateMachine disabled' log lines with what the kernel does with the NCM interface.
